original_value: AbstractThe growth of Learning Analytics (LA) as a research field has been extensively documented since its beginnings. This paper provides a broad overview of the publications that Latin American authors have published in the last years by performing a quantitative review of the literature (from 2011 to 2019). A total of 282 papers were collected and categorized according to a multidimensional model composed of seven dimensions (data collected, stakeholders targeted, goals of the paper, techniques employed, maturity of the tool, research approaches and ethical issues). The paper describes how the field has evolved over the years in Latin America, presenting the main characteristics of the papers from different perspectives (year, type of venue, language) together with the descriptives of the categorized dimensions and the relations between them. At last, papers are presented in number by countries and institutions, and we perform an authorship and coauthorship analysis with information extracted from the selected papers.

result.paraphrase: This paper offers a wide-ranging review of publications by Latin American authors in recent years through a quantitative literature review covering 2011 to 2019. It gathered 282 papers and organized them using a multidimensional model with seven dimensions: data collected, targeted stakeholders, paper goals, employed techniques, tool maturity, research approaches, and ethical issues. The study outlines how learning analytics has developed in Latin America over time, examining the papers from multiple angles, including year, venue type, and language, alongside descriptions of the categorized dimensions and their interrelationships. Finally, it reports paper counts by country and institution and carries out authorship and coauthorship analyses based on the selected papers.
